openQuestions.q: CHK-004 userSees says "english-open-source-surface PASSES standalone (no CJK flagged)", but the main agents own investigation confirmed 4 CJK sources remain intentionally unfixed: (a) packages/main/src/handlers/agent-prompt.ts and (b) packages/main/src/handlers/validate-docs-drift.ts are production files in ALLOWLIST_PENDING_SOURCE_MIGRATION (pending translation, not yet translated), and (c) packages/main/src/tasks/docs-drift-path-drift-smoke.ts and (d) packages/main/src/tasks/prompt-token-cost-smoke.ts are test files with functional CJK fixtures in ALLOWLIST_TEST_GLOBS. If the implementer reads userSees literally ("no CJK flagged") they may conclude the smoke must pass with zero CJK hits anywhere, and then either (i) extend the content fix beyond usage-ledger-estimate-smoke.ts (scope creep into production files) or (ii) weaken/remove the allowlist to make it pass cleanly — either of which violates the guardrail. The question is: does the CHK-004 acceptance criterion require the implementer to verify only that the smoke PASSES (i.e., the allowlist correctly handles the 4 out-of-scope CJK sources so the smoke does not fail on them) — or does it also require that no CJK is reported/flagged in any allowlisted file? If the allowlist mechanism makes the smoke pass despite those 4 files being allowlisted, is that sufficient, or must the implementer translate/remove those files too?
